story: Ebenezer Baptist Church was founded in 1886 by Pastor John A. Parker and eight people on Airline Street.
The church building was dedicated in 1922. Martin Luther King Jr. served as co-pastor with his father from 1960 until his assassination in 1968, and his funeral was held at Ebenezer on April 9, 1968.
The newer Horizon Sanctuary was inaugurated in 1999 with 1,700 seats, in the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park.
stops.fact: The church was founded with nine people.
stops.disputed: Wikipedia does not give the national park's founding year or the old sanctuary's style, so check the park's own history before repeating them.

claims.t: Ebenezer Baptist Church was founded in 1886.
claims.why: Wikipedia: founded in 1886 by Pastor John A. Parker.
1968 is the year of King's funeral. It was founded in 1886.

story: Centennial Olympic Park was built for the 1996 Summer Olympics by the Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games. Billy Payne, the chief executive, came up with it. Phase I opened in July 1996, and Phase II was finished in 1998.
The Fountain of Rings has 251 jets that shoot 12 to 35 feet high, with computer-controlled lights and water synchronized to music. Shows run four times a day.

Visitors could buy a brick for $35 with a message of up to 15 characters on two lines. About 800,000 bricks were used. The park replaced vacant lots and run-down industrial buildings, and the Georgia Aquarium and the World of Coca-Cola are on its north side.
stops.fact: The park's pavers are engraved with donor messages.
stops.disputed: Sources give the park as 21 or 22 acres. Wikipedia's article uses both.

claims.t: Centennial Olympic Park was built for the 1996 Games.
claims.why: Wikipedia: built by ACOG for the 1996 Summer Olympics.
Donors paid $35 for an engraved message on each brick.

stops.name: Fox Theatre
stops.teaser: A theater that was almost torn down, saved by the people of Atlanta.
stops.map: Fox Theatre, 660 Peachtree St NE, Atlanta, GA
stops.clue: Go to Peachtree Street in Midtown and find the grand theater with the striped towers and domes that look like a mosque.
stops.safety: Peachtree Street is a busy road. Use crosswalks and watch for event crowds.

story: The Fox was planned as the Yaarab Temple of the Shriners and shared with William Fox's theater. Construction ran from 1925 to 1929, and it opened on Christmas Day 1929. Marye, Alger and Vinour were the architects.

It uses Islamic and Egyptian decorative motifs. The auditorium was designed as an Arab-style courtyard under a night sky, with 96 bulbs and a projector that moved clouds across the ceiling. The Mighty Mo organ has 3,622 pipes.

In 1974 Southern Bell planned to tear down the closed theater. The Save the Fox campaign formed, Mayor Maynard Jackson imposed an eight-month moratorium on demolition, and the Fox was listed on the National Register that year.
stops.disputed: Do not mix up the Fox in Atlanta with the Fox Theatre in Detroit. Both are old movie palaces with different histories.

claims.t: The Fox Theatre in Atlanta was saved from demolition in the 1970s.
claims.why: Wikipedia: the Save the Fox campaign began in 1974.
It opened on Christmas Day 1929. 1974 is the year of the demolition threat.

stops.teaser: A garden cemetery that survived the Civil War, with a famous author's grave.
stops.map: Oakland Cemetery, 248 Oakland Ave SE, Atlanta, GA
stops.clue: Go to the Victorian cemetery just southeast of downtown. Find the brick Bell Tower near the entrance.
stops.safety: It is a place of rest. Stay on paths, do not touch or rub the markers, and be quiet.

story: Oakland Cemetery started in 1850 as Atlanta Cemetery on six acres and was renamed in 1872 for its oaks and magnolias. It now covers 48 acres in the Victorian garden style.

Margaret Mitchell, author of Gone with the Wind, golfer Bobby Jones and former mayor Maynard Jackson are buried there. Many African American graves were marked with wood, which decayed, so a lot of graves are unidentified.

Most of Atlanta burned in 1864, but the original six acres survived. The Bell Tower was built in 1899 and now houses the visitor center. The Historic Oakland Foundation restores graves and offers tours.
stops.fact: General Hood watched the Battle of Atlanta from near the Bell Tower.
stops.disputed: The Confederate section holds about 6,900 burials, and roughly 3,000 are unknown. Read counts carefully, because they differ by section.

claims.why: Wikipedia: established in 1850 as Atlanta Cemetery.
It began in 1850. 1864 is the year of the Battle of Atlanta.
